title: Forward Deployed Engineer - EMEA
descriptionHtml:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

About the role

You embed directly with customer teams as the engineer on the ground: own an outcome, ship a production-grade SpaceXAI system that still runs after you leave, and become the critical technical feedback loop from the field back to product engineering.

The work is the project. One week you might take a messy business workflow and put a production agent on it: pick the use case, stand up the architecture, wire it into the customer’s auth, data, and tools, then harden it with evals until the team actually uses it. Another week you might live in a customer’s repo and delivery system and ship an agent-powered path for a migration, a PR review loop, or an incident-to-fix flow, behind tests, review, and rollout rather than in a chat sidebar. Either way, you measure what matters, leave the customer able to operate it, and bring the pattern back as another use case for SpaceXAI.

This is not a demo role. You own the work end to end, from the first discovery call through launch, iteration, and post-launch support, and you are responsible for systems that work in the real world.

What you’ll do

  • Lead discovery with the customer: orient in their codebases and workflows, find the real bottleneck and the use case worth building, and define clear success metrics

  • Design and ship production agents, AI applications, and coding-agent workflows on Grok and our models, on live business processes and inside the customer’s engineering org

  • Get a first version live in days, then harden it over weeks with rollout, monitoring, and iteration from real usage

  • Own production quality: tracing, evals, debugging model or delivery failures, and latency and cost tradeoffs

  • Build the systems around the model (tools, MCP servers, retrieval, rules, skills, CI gates, and evals) and integrate them into the customer’s auth, data, workflow, and delivery systems; decide when prompting, architecture, data, process, or a model change is the right lever

  • Measure the outcome that matters (revenue, cost, hours saved, error rate, cycle time, escaped defects), not seat adoption

  • Work directly with Staff+, platform, and domain leaders, going deep in their systems while communicating clearly about tradeoffs and results

  • Leave the customer team able to run what you built, and turn what you learn into reusable patterns and improvements to SpaceXAI products

You may be a fit if

Required

  • You have 5+ years of experience in software engineering, machine learning engineering, or data science

  • You write and review production code (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript; other languages welcome)

  • You’ve owned a customer or operator outcome, not just a slide or a prototype, and can turn a fuzzy problem into a scoped, shipped system

  • You’ve built and owned AI-native workflows or agents in production, and debugged real production failures (model, tool, data, pipeline, or delivery path)

  • You’ve handled production reliability: metrics, alerts, safe rollouts, incident response

  • You build end to end: frontend, backend, infra, and prompt iteration

  • You thrive in ambiguity and don’t need a complete spec before you start building

  • You can talk to working engineers and to a VP

Nice to have

  • 2+ years in a customer-facing role, leading discovery conversations and being accountable for outcomes for external stakeholders

  • Hands-on depth in several of: agents and tool-calling, eval harnesses, retrieval and context systems, CI/CD or developer platforms, and AI-native coding workflows in a real repo

  • Experience as a forward-deployed, solutions, or platform engineer embedded with customers, or as a founding engineer who owned an AI product end to end

Our Sales Development team partners closely with Growth, Marketing, RevOps, and Sales to identify buying signals, engage customers at the right moment, and create highly personalized outreach informed by product usage, PLG signals, and creative automation. You’ll help your team balance modern, signal-based engagement with disciplined outbound prospecting to consistently create new opportunities across commercial and enterprise accounts.

You’ll be responsible for building a strong team culture, driving execution against pipeline goals, coaching early-career talent, and continuously improving how SpaceXAI engages prospective customers across APJ. This role is ideal for a hands-on sales leader who enjoys coaching people, experimenting with new approaches, and building scalable operating rhythms in a fast-growing company.

 

This is a full-time, in-office leadership role based in our Singapore office.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Hire, onboard, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Account Associates supporting the APJ business.

  • Lead the team’s day-to-day execution against pipeline generation goals, activity metrics, and conversion targets.

  • Help define and refine regional sales development playbooks that combine modern automation with highly personalized customer engagement.

  • Coach Account Associates on prospecting, discovery, qualification, messaging, and customer engagement to consistently improve pipeline quality.

  • Establish a strong operating cadence through regular pipeline reviews, one-on-ones, performance coaching, team meetings, and career development.

  • Monitor team performance, identify trends, and use data to continuously improve productivity, conversion rates, and execution.

  • Collaborate closely with Commercial and Enterprise Sales leaders to ensure high-quality pipeline generation and seamless opportunity handoffs.

  • Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation, accountability, and continuous learning.

  • Develop future sales talent by creating clear career pathways into Account Executive and other GTM roles across SpaceXAI.

     

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of SaaS sales experience, including experience leading frontline Sales Development or SDR teams.

  • Proven success hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing SDRs or Account Associates in a fast-paced technology company.

  • Experience building predictable outbound pipeline generation through a combination of prospecting, automation, and data-driven experimentation.

  • Strong operational discipline with experience managing team performance through metrics, coaching, and structured operating cadences.

  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with Marketing, Growth, RevOps, and Sales to improve pipeline generation and conversion.

  • Passion for coaching and developing early-career sales talent into successful GTM professionals.

  • Curiosity about AI, developer tools, or technical products, with the ability to help teams engage technical buyers effectively.

  • Comfortable operating in a high-growth, fast-changing environment where experimentation and continuous improvement are expected.

  • Excellent communication, coaching, and leadership skills with a collaborative, builder’s mindset.

  • Experience with AI products, growth automation platforms, PLG motions, or developer-focused technology is a plus.

About the role

We’re hiring Solution Architects to help the world’s best engineering organizations figure out what AI-native software development actually looks like in production.

This is a deeply technical, post-sale role embedded inside SpaceXSI’s most strategic enterprise accounts. You’ll work directly with engineering teams to roll out high-impact workflows, accelerate adoption, and help organizations fundamentally rethink how software gets built with AI.

Solution Architects sit at the center of long-term customer transformation. You’ll help customers move from initial excitement to deeply integrating engineering workflows that teams rely on every day. That means understanding how modern software organizations operate, identifying where the Grok platform can create the most leverage, and helping customers scale adoption across teams, platforms, and workflows over time.

This role is highly hands-on. You’ll configure environments, design workflows, run enablement sessions, and solve technical problems directly with developers and platform teams inside complex enterprise environments. You’ll also help engineering leaders think through rollout strategy, workflow evolution, and the long-term architecture for AI-native development.

The best Solution Architects combine deep technical credibility with strong product instincts, high ownership, and the ability to influence how large engineering organizations evolve. Solution Architects are also equally comfortable debugging CI workflows, leading architecture reviews, and helping executives understand where AI changes the economics of software development.

 

What you'll do

Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development

  • Roll out Grok, Grokbot, and Grok Build across strategic engineering organizations

  • Configure environments, design workflows, and run hands-on enablement sessions

  • Help developers integrate Grok into real production workflows, not isolated demos

  • Drive fast time-to-value and durable adoption across teams

  • Identify workflow friction and solve problems quickly

Expand Cursor Across the Organization

  • Identify where Grok should expand next inside the customer environment

  • Help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption

  • Design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups

  • Partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale

  • Work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments

Become a Trusted Technical Partner

  • Build deep relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering leadership, and executive stakeholders

  • Lead architecture reviews, technical working sessions, and strategic planning discussions

  • Advise customers on developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and AI adoption strategy

  • Coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to unblock customer progress

  • Help organizations navigate workflow and operational change as AI-native development evolves

Drive Real Customer Outcomes

  • Help customers translate adoption into measurable engineering impact

  • Connect Grok usage to outcomes like faster iteration cycles, improved developer productivity, workflow efficiency, and engineering quality

  • Help customers communicate the value of Grok internally and build momentum for broader adoption

  • Turn successful deployments into repeatable workflow patterns across the organization

Help Make Cursor Indispensable

  • Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness

  • Monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on Grok over time

  • Support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction

  • Help customers build workflows they can’t imagine operating without

Shape the Future of the Product

  • Bring structured feedback from strategic customers into Product and Engineering

  • Identify emerging workflow patterns, friction points, and enterprise requirements

  • Help shape new capabilities through lighthouse customers and design partnerships

  • Turn successful customer workflows into reusable playbooks and reference patterns

     

You may be a fit if

  • You have a strong technical background in software engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, or developer tooling

  • You have experience in customer-facing technical roles such as Solution Architect, Solutions Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Enterprise Architect, or similar

  • You have the ability to work hands-on with engineering teams while also operating strategically with technical leadership

  • You have a strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, integrations, CI/CD systems, governance, and enterprise engineering environments

  • You have excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly across both technical and executive audiences

  • You have strong instincts around workflow design, adoption strategy, and driving workflow change across engineering teams

  • You have high ownership, strong execution skills, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments with ambiguity

  • You have a passion for developer tooling and strong conviction around how AI will reshape software engineering

  • You are willing to travel to customers needed

You'll help run the campaigns that create demand for our products among enterprise buyers building programs for priority accounts, crafting stories that land with our target audiences, and executing the webinars, offers, nurture, and campaign deliverables that turn engagement into pipeline.

This is an execution-heavy role with plenty of room to grow. You'll write the copy and execute the programs that carry each campaign, and bring a data-driven mindset to drive continuous optimization. It's a high-agency position for someone who loves to ship, wants to learn fast, and wants a direct line to revenue.

This is an SF-based role and requires regular presence in our San Francisco office.

What you'll do

  • Build and run programs for priority accounts and segments.

    • Design and run ABM programs for clusters of strategic accounts grouped by vertical, tech stack, use case, or buying-group pattern, with messaging, content, and offers tailored to each cluster, in partnership with sales, SDRs, and field marketing.

    • Scale what works into 1:many programmatic plays across a broader target list of prospects and customers, using intent, enrichment, and ad targeting to reach the right buying groups without hand-building every touch.

    • Map buying centers inside each account (VP Eng, CTO, platform and developer experience leads, security and procurement) and build multithreaded plays that reach each of them.

    • Turn account intelligence, intent, and usage signals into tailored campaign treatments, from personalized outreach and executive programs to events, direct mail, and sales plays.

  • Tell stories that land with technical buyers.

    • Shape the narrative, messaging, and offers for each campaign, and write the copy that carries it: briefs, emails, landing pages, ads, and account-specific content.

    • Develop engaging concepts and formats for virtual events (webinars, workshops, and exec roundtables), owning all aspects of production from idea to follow-up: select relevant topics, line up speakers from internal leaders and our customers, and make sure everyone is prepared.

    • Brief design and creative partners clearly and keep the story consistent across every channel and touchpoint.

  • Conceptualize and deploy creative demand gen offers

    • Come up with offers that give target accounts a reason to engage, like meeting makers, direct mail, digital engagement programs, and gifting.

    • Work with sales and SDRs on who gets each offer and how they follow up, and manage vendors on fulfillment, shipping, and budget.

    • Track every offer from send to meeting to pipeline so we know what to repeat.

  • Build thoughtful email campaigns and nurture programs

    • Develop and improve nurture sequences for prospects and customers, segmented by persona, account tier, and where they are in the journey.

    • Write and edit email copy, analyze performance, and come up with new ideas for content angles and CTAs that improve engagement.

    • Partner with our lifecycle and email owners to keep lists clean, segments accurate, and every send on brand.

  • Execute the deliverables that bring campaigns to life.

    • Turn campaign plans into finished work: write briefs for design, and build landing pages, emails, ads, and sales one-pagers.

    • Own launch checklists and timelines, coordinate with design, web, ops, and sales, and ship on time.

    • Report on how each campaign performed, share what you learned with the team and sales, and suggest what to try next.

You may be a fit if

  • You're both left-brained and right-brained: as comfortable debating pipeline math as you are coming up with a creative campaign idea.

  • You write well. You can tell a compelling story, write copy that makes a busy engineering leader keep reading, and you have strong instincts for what good looks like.

  • You've supported ABM or integrated campaigns and understand the basics of account selection, buying groups, and multithreading in enterprise deals.

  • You're organized and detail-oriented, and you can juggle many deliverables and deadlines without dropping any.

  • You like working closely with sales, and you know how to earn trust with sellers.

  • You want ownership and high agency, and you'd rather ship and learn than wait for perfect information.

  • You can take a loose plan, bring structure to it, and get it shipped.

  • You're curious about AI and developer tools, and you use AI in your own workflow every day.

Experience that helps

  • 3 to 5 years in B2B marketing, demand generation, or marketing operations, with hands-on time supporting ABM or integrated campaigns for enterprise or technical audiences.

  • Hands-on experience running webinars, direct mail or meeting-maker programs, and email nurture.

  • Familiarity with tools like Salesforce, a marketing automation platform, webinar platforms, direct mail or gifting platforms, and Clay or ABM and intent platforms. Bonus if you've used AI coding tools to query data yourself.

  • Experience with verticalized or persona-specific go-to-market motions.

  • A track record of campaigns you can point to with real results, and the writing samples to back it up.

You'll work directly with engineering teams to roll out high-impact workflows, accelerate adoption, and help organizations fundamentally rethink how software gets built with AI. Solution Architects sit at the center of long-term customer transformation.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development: Roll out SpaceXSI across strategic engineering organizations; configure environments, design workflows, and run hands-on enablement sessions; help developers integrate SpaceXSI into real production workflows, not isolated demos; drive fast time-to-value and durable adoption across teams; identify workflow friction and solve problems quickly

  • Expand SpaceXSI Across the Organization: Identify where SpaceXSI should expand next inside the customer environment; help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption; design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups; partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale; work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments

  • Become a Trusted Technical Partner: Build deep relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering leadership, and executive stakeholders; lead architecture reviews, technical working sessions, and strategic planning discussions; advise customers on developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and AI adoption strategy; coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to unblock customer progress; help organizations navigate workflow and operational change as AI-native development evolves

  • Drive Real Customer Outcomes: Help customers translate adoption into measurable engineering impact; connect SpaceXSI usage to outcomes like faster iteration cycles, improved developer productivity, workflow efficiency, and engineering quality; help customers communicate the value of SpaceXSI internally and build momentum for broader adoption; turn successful deployments into repeatable workflow patterns across the organization

  • Help Make SpaceXSI Indispensable: Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness; monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on SpaceXSI over time; support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction; help customers build workflows they can't imagine operating without

  • Shape the Future of the Product: Bring structured feedback from strategic customers into Product and Engineering; identify emerging workflow patterns, friction points, and enterprise requirements; help shape new capabilities through lighthouse customers and design partnerships; turn successful customer workflows into reusable playbooks and reference patterns

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Technical background in software engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, or developer tooling

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role such as Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Enterprise Architect, or similar

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • The ability to work hands-on with engineering teams while also operating strategically with technical leadership

  • A strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, integrations, CI/CD systems, governance, and enterprise engineering environments

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly across both technical and executive audiences

  • Strong instincts around workflow design, adoption strategy, and driving workflow change across engineering teams

  • High ownership, strong execution skills, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments with ambiguity

  • A passion for developer tooling and strong conviction around how AI will reshape software engineering

About the role

As a Product Engineer on the Grok Connectors team at SpaceXAI, you'll build the integrations that let Grok, Cursor and Grok Bot do real work inside the tools people use every day: Gmail, Outlook, Google Calendar and Drive, Microsoft Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint, GitHub, Slack, finance accounts, and a fast-growing marketplace of third-party MCP plugins. You'll architect, implement, and deploy features end to end, from OAuth sign-in and token handling, to tool schemas and reliability across hundreds of millions of tool calls, to the cards and approval flows users see on web, desktop, and mobile. You'll work directly with enterprise customers and partners to ship connectors that large organizations can trust.

You may be a fit if

  • You have an entrepreneurial spirit and love creating outsized business impact.

  • You want AI agents to be genuinely useful, by connecting them to real data and real actions safely.

  • You have deep, practical knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC and of large provider APIs like Google Workspace and Microsoft Graph, or you're excited to become the expert.

  • You care about reliability: concurrency, retries, rate limits, and observability. You fix root causes, not symptoms.

  • You let data decide what to work on. You size user impact from logs and metrics, and you measure error rates before and after every fix.

  • You're strong in TypeScript and comfortable shipping across backend services and client UI in a large codebase.

  • You enjoy working with customers, partners, QA, and support, and can answer a security review question as clearly as you can fix a bug.

  • Bonus: experience with the MCP protocol, Rust, Kubernetes and multi-cloud deployments, enterprise security and compliance (ZDR, audit logs, Conditional Access), or building LLM agents for automation.

Sample projects include

  • Building an automated triage system that pulls user reports from feedback channels, groups them by root cause with user-impact estimates, files issues, and starts a first-pass coding agent on each fix

  • Redesigning OAuth token refresh so concurrent requests never burn a single-use refresh token and mark a working connector as disconnected

  • Cutting hundreds of thousands of daily tool-call errors by generating tool definitions from vendors' published API specs, fixing argument mapping, and adding batch tools

  • Shipping Gmail and Outlook draft, reply, and attachment flows, with approval cards so an agent never sends an email without the user's sign-off

  • Launching new partner connectors, from debugging a partner's OAuth metadata to rollout and adoption metrics

  • Making connectors work for enterprise and single-tenant deployments: custom certificate authorities, Entra Conditional Access, admin controls, and compliance reviews with large financial institutions

Applying

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

  • Own the founder funnel and footprint: Deploy a mix of founder events, hackathons, executive/founder roundtables, and community activations to acquire the right startups and drive them toward meaningful success using Cursor.

title: Sr. Research Engineer, Synthetic Data
descriptionHtml:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

Research Engineer, Synthetic Data

About the Role

As a Sr. Research Engineer on the Synth Data team at SpaceXAI, you’ll invent and scale the synthetic data that teaches our models new capabilities. You own the full loop: spotting a capability the model is missing, designing a data generation strategy, building reliable pipelines and verifiers, and validating that the resulting data actually moves the model.

You form hypotheses about what data will help, build the systems to produce it at scale, run ablations, and read the resulting traces and training signals to understand why it worked (or didn’t). Your datasets go directly into frontier training runs, and shape the development of Grok models.

What you’ll work on

  • Designing end-to-end synthetic data recipes that turn raw sources (traces, documents, codebases, workflows) into large, diverse, verifiable task sets.

  • Building strong verification and anti-hacking mechanisms so rewards are simple to compute and hard to game.

  • Controlling difficulty and diversity so data stays learnable and reflects real usage instead of collapsing into templates.

  • Running targeted ablations and analyses that demonstrate a dataset caused a capability improvement (and ruling out grader or data artifacts).

  • Iterating from traces and training results to close specific gaps, then turning successful one-off recipes into reusable infrastructure.

  • Partnering with research and other RL Data teams to translate model capability goals into concrete synthetic data plans.

You may be a fit if

  • You have research experience on synthetic or post-training data, in industry or academia. You've designed a data generation method, shipped the data into training, and can show its impact to the model you’re training.

  • You have strong software engineering fundamentals and have built non-trivial data pipelines, agent systems, or evaluation frameworks.

  • You have taste for what makes a good training task: hard enough to teach something real, simple enough to grade reliably, and resistant to reward hacking.

  • You are careful and systematic — understanding both aggregate metrics and close reading of raw outputs.

  • You enjoy turning messy, open-ended problems into repeatable, high-quality data production systems.

Applying

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
descriptionHtml:

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

About the role

You embed directly with customer teams as the engineer on the ground: own an outcome, ship a production-grade SpaceXAI system that still runs after you leave, and become the critical technical feedback loop from the field back to product engineering.

The work is the project. One week you might take a messy business workflow and put a production agent on it: pick the use case, stand up the architecture, wire it into the customer’s auth, data, and tools, then harden it with evals until the team actually uses it. Another week you might live in a customer’s repo and delivery system and ship an agent-powered path for a migration, a PR review loop, or an incident-to-fix flow, behind tests, review, and rollout rather than in a chat sidebar. Either way, you measure what matters, leave the customer able to operate it, and bring the pattern back as another use case for SpaceXAI.

This is not a demo role. You own the work end to end, from the first discovery call through launch, iteration, and post-launch support, and you are responsible for systems that work in the real world.

What you’ll do

  • Lead discovery with the customer: orient in their codebases and workflows, find the real bottleneck and the use case worth building, and define clear success metrics

  • Design and ship production agents, AI applications, and coding-agent workflows on Grok and our models, on live business processes and inside the customer’s engineering org

  • Get a first version live in days, then harden it over weeks with rollout, monitoring, and iteration from real usage

  • Own production quality: tracing, evals, debugging model or delivery failures, and latency and cost tradeoffs

  • Build the systems around the model (tools, MCP servers, retrieval, rules, skills, CI gates, and evals) and integrate them into the customer’s auth, data, workflow, and delivery systems; decide when prompting, architecture, data, process, or a model change is the right lever

  • Measure the outcome that matters (revenue, cost, hours saved, error rate, cycle time, escaped defects), not seat adoption

  • Work directly with Staff+, platform, and domain leaders, going deep in their systems while communicating clearly about tradeoffs and results

  • Leave the customer team able to run what you built, and turn what you learn into reusable patterns and improvements to SpaceXAI products

You may be a fit if

  • You have 5+ years of experience in software engineering, machine learning engineering, or data science

  • You write and review production code (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript; other languages welcome)

  • You’ve owned a customer or operator outcome, not just a slide or a prototype, and can turn a fuzzy problem into a scoped, shipped system

  • You’ve built and owned AI-native workflows or agents in production, and debugged real production failures (model, tool, data, pipeline, or delivery path)

  • You’ve handled production reliability: metrics, alerts, safe rollouts, incident response

  • You build end to end: frontend, backend, infra, and prompt iteration

  • You thrive in ambiguity and don’t need a complete spec before you start building

  • You can talk to working engineers and to a VP

Nice to have

  • 2+ years in a customer-facing role, leading discovery conversations and being accountable for outcomes for external stakeholders

  • Hands-on depth in several of: agents and tool-calling, eval harnesses, retrieval and context systems, CI/CD or developer platforms, and AI-native coding workflows in a real repo

  • Experience as a forward-deployed, solutions, or platform engineer embedded with customers, or as a founding engineer who owned an AI product end to end

descriptionHtml:

About the role

Lifecycle Growth's job is to get more people using Grok, Grok Bot, X, Cursor and the API every day, and to turn that use into revenue. We own everything after signup: getting people to value, converting them to paid, growing their teams and keeping them coming back. We do it with lifecycle marketing, in-product messaging and a steady stream of experiments, and much of the work runs on agents we build ourselves.

This isn't a traditional marketing role. You'll do the work of a product manager, a product marketer and a marketing engineer, often in the same day. You'll own lifecycle growth for one or more of our products. You'll figure out where the biggest opportunity is, design the program, build it and show whether it actually moved the number.

The job spans consumer and business, self-serve and sales-led, so you'll need to think as clearly about a solo user's first week as about a team's path to an enterprise deal. You'll go deep on the systems underneath, like who's eligible, what triggers a message, how events and attributes are modeled, and how data moves from the warehouse into our messaging tools. When the best fix lives in the product or the data, you'll make the case and either build it yourself or work with engineering to ship it.

This is an in-person role based in our San Francisco office.

What you’ll do

  • Strategy and roadmap: Own lifecycle end to end across our suite of products: Grok, Grok Bot, X, Cursor and the API, from activation and conversion to paid through team expansion, retention and winback.

  • Data and audiences: Use SQL and product data to size opportunities, build the audiences and triggers behind each program, and prove what actually drove revenue.

  • Journeys: Architect multi-step, cross-channel programs across email, push and in-app, with event-based triggers, branching and suppression logic, and personalization drawn from product usage, plan and billing state, and company and role enrichment.

  • Systems: Drive and continuously improve the data model lifecycle runs on, including identity, events, attributes and eligibility, and partner with engineering on the warehouse syncs, APIs and webhooks that keep it accurate in real time.

  • Measurement: Run every program as an experiment with a proper holdout, measure incremental lift, and make judgment calls when a result is inconclusive.

  • Portfolio: Manage lifecycle as a portfolio of programs, putting more behind what works and retiring what doesn't.

  • In-product: Own in-product messaging and experiments, from onboarding and upgrade prompts to post-purchase plan tours, and partner with product and engineering to improve our in-app comms systems.

  • Tooling: Use code and agents to build the internal tools, templates and automated QA the team runs on, so each new program ships faster than the last.

You may be a fit if

  • 8+ years in Lifecycle, Growth PMM or Product Growth at a high-growth product company.

  • The range to think fluently about lifecycle for consumers and businesses, self-serve and sales-led, and to know how each one changes the right move.

  • Real technical depth. You write SQL, you know how events, identity and attributes fit together, and you're comfortable with APIs, webhooks and warehouse syncs. Coding is a plus.

  • Hands-on experience running complex programs in a major lifecycle platform, such as Braze, Customer.io or Iterable.

  • A history of building lifecycle systems with engineering, not just running campaigns on top of them.

  • Programs you can point to that moved revenue, paid users or retention, with holdouts to back it up.

  • Good experimentation judgment, focused on incrementality, cohort quality and lifetime value rather than opens and clicks.

  • Experience shipping in-product messaging or experiments alongside product and engineering.

  • The ability to set direction, bring product, engineering, data and design with you, and explain your thinking clearly to leadership.

  • A habit of using AI agents and code to get more done than a team your size should.

This role requires being in-office in San Francisco.

This team makes sure the right data, in the right form, hits the training clusters on time and at the quality bar required to push the scaling curve. This is done by building our own models, our own high-performance pipelines, and by running the experiments that prove the data is actually stellar.

  • The Data Platform Team owns the infrastructure and pipelines that transform raw data dumps into training-ready datasets. This team improves the speed, reliability, and developer experience of our initial training data pipelines so researchers can quickly experiment with new data sources, quality filters, taxonomies, multimodal data, and data mixes that improve model performance.

  • The Crawling team owns large-scale web crawling and parsing that feeds the top of the funnel for initial training. They discover, schedule, fetch, and parse public web content so high-quality documents become the raw scrapes that Data Quality and Data Platform turn into tokens and mixes. This is deep distributed systems work with real ownership: host coverage and prioritization, fetch success under antibot and trap content, HTML/document parsing quality, and reliability of the crawl infrastructure that must continuously supply every downstream data pipeline.

What you’ll do

  • on the Data Quality Team:

    • Build and own high-throughput, fully telemetered data pipelines that process frontier-scale data with end-to-end traceability. If something breaks or drifts, your systems will tell us before the training run does.

    • Train and ship models that classify, rank, filter, clean, and identify data at extreme throughput. These models have to be both accurate and fast enough to sit in the critical path without becoming the bottleneck.

    • Design and run scaling-ladder experiments on data-mixture, repeatability, and quality depth that turn “this dataset feels good” into hard evidence the training team can trust.

    • Partner tightly with Data Acquisition to hunt down missing or low-quality sources, and with the training teams to close the loop on what actually moves loss and downstream evals.

    • Treat data quality as a systems problem and a research problem. You will write performance-critical code one week and design careful experiments the next.

  • on the Data Platform Team:

    • Build the platform that turns raw web, code, multimodal, and acquired data into training-ready datasets for frontier pretraining runs.

    • Own the pipelines, orchestration, and tooling that make pretraining data iteration fast, reliable, observable, and reproducible at scale.

    • Create clear signals for data quality, lineage, freshness, and pipeline health so researchers can trust what goes into each run.

    • Partner with initial training, crawling, data quality, and acquisition teams to turn new data ideas into measurable improvements in loss, evals, and model capability.

  • on the Crawling Team:

    • Build and scale the web crawling systems that discover, schedule, fetch, and parse high-quality documents across the open web for initial training.

    • Improve URL seeding, scoring, and fair host scheduling so crawl capacity lands on the hosts and pages that matter most for model quality.

    • Raise crawl success and parsing quality — defeating antibot failures, improving extractors, and capturing content we previously could not get cleanly.

    • Debug and harden complex crawl infrastructure end-to-end for availability, recovery, and ingestion lag, and automate delivery of crawl datasets into the data pipeline.

    • Work independently (and alongside AI agents) and partner with Data Quality and Data Platform so new coverage shows up as better tokens in training runs.

You may be a fit if

  • You have a strong infrastructure or data platform background, and ideally a spike of outlier depth somewhere (crawling/search infra is a plus, not a hard requirement)

  • You are a high-slope engineer who has moved unusually fast — for example, staff-level ownership within a few years — or you bring deep domain experience

  • You are able to architect and ship end-to-end with high ownership, debug complex systems independently, and work alongside AI agents

  • You have strong intuitions about large-scale distributed systems

  • You’re excited to learn how pre-training data shapes model quality, and want the ownership and visibility that comes with building systems that feed frontier training runs

title: Engineering Manager, Agent & Product Security
descriptionHtml:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

About the role

Cursor’s agents work inside the codebases of some of the most security-conscious engineering organizations in the world — holding credentials, reading untrusted content, running tools, and shipping changes. Today they act on authority delegated per task. Where we’re headed, they’ll work more like coworkers: autonomous over long horizons, holding standing responsibilities, initiating work, and collaborating with people and other agents. The security models that future needs — identity and accountability for autonomous workers, standing authority rather than per-task permission, agent-to-agent trust, oversight that scales with always-on autonomy — mostly don’t exist yet.

As Engineering Manager for Agent & Product Security, you’ll lead the team that makes agentic software development trustworthy. This team owns the security boundaries between customers, data, tools, repositories, workspaces, and agent authority across Cursor’s product and agents and designs the primitives behind them: agent identity, delegated authority, policy enforcement, secure tool execution, and prompt-injection containment. Little of this has settled precedent, so the team’s decisions carry unusual weight for Cursor and for how the industry approaches these problems.

Security here is tightly coupled to product strategy: customers adopt agent autonomy as fast as we can make it trustworthy, so the boundaries your team makes safe directly determine what the product can ship. You’ll help set that direction.

What you’ll do

  • Chart the path from supervised agents to trusted autonomous ones: define the security primitives that enable agent autonomy, and lead the team that builds them.

  • Engineer the isolation that makes Cursor safe to run inside customers’ most valuable codebases: tenancy, workspace, secret, and data protections designed for real adversaries.

  • Build the authority infrastructure autonomous agents need: identity, scoped permissions, policy enforcement, and secure tool execution, so an agent can hold real responsibility with verifiable limits and full accountability.

  • Build customer-facing security controls that are understandable, usable, and strong enough for Cursor’s most security-sensitive customers, with crisp success metrics for security outcomes.

  • Hire, coach, and grow a high-performing security engineering team while staying technically close to the work: write and review code where useful, and keep execution fast and technically grounded.

You may be a fit if

  • You’ve led engineering teams shipping production systems with high security, reliability, or platform stakes — and you want a problem space where much of the answer isn’t written down yet.

  • You have strong product and systems judgment: you can reason from user workflows to architecture, threat models, enforcement points, and operational tradeoffs — and you see security as something that enables product capability, not only restricts it.

  • You understand modern application security, authorization, tenancy, identity, secrets, data isolation, and secure-by-default platform design.

  • You have good instincts about AI agents: how they use tools, where authority should come from, how prompt injection and exfiltration show up in practice, and how to build mitigations that hold up against creative adversaries.

  • You’re comfortable operating in ambiguity: you can set strategy where precedent is thin, commit to a direction, and stay close enough to the implementation to know when to change it.

  • You can partner well across product, infrastructure, ML, and customer-facing teams.

About the role

We're hiring a Software Engineer, Billing to evolve the systems that power how Cursor charges and reconciles revenue across millions of developers and enterprise teams.

You will work across the billing stack — usage metering pipelines, subscription and entitlement systems, payment integrations, and the ledger layer — to make billing accurate, scalable, and transparent. This is a deeply technical IC role. It is not a finance ops role, and it is not a backend generalist role wearing a billing hat.

What you’ll do

  • Implement usage and billing systems changes end-to-end, from updates in the UI and raw usage events at the edge to invoiced amounts in Stripe, including the metering pipeline, aggregation logic, entitlement enforcement, and ledger.

  • Evolve our ledger system that serves as the source of truth for customer balances, credits, overages, and adjustments — with the correctness guarantees that financial systems require.

  • Integrate deeply with Stripe including subscriptions, usage records, invoices, webhooks, and edge cases like mid-cycle plan changes, prorations, and failed payment recovery.

  • Build billing APIs and internal tooling that product, finance, and customer success teams depend on to query customer state, issue credits, and investigate billing anomalies.

  • Improve observability across the billing pipeline — metering lag, reconciliation discrepancies, invoice accuracy — so the team can quickly detect and debug billing regressions.

  • Partner with product, infrastructure, and finance teams to ship new pricing models with confidence and minimal operational risk.

  • You will own usage & limits across the product family, payments (stripe + daily jobs), grants & promotions, ledger, and internal data insights. You will be a technical authority on billing correctness and scale.

  • You will not own tax compliance, or general finance infrastructure unless it intersects directly with the billing system.

  • You will not be a backend generalist who contributes to billing occasionally. This is the core of your scope.

  • Revenue accuracy is part of the job, but the goal is to build systems with enough correctness and observability that billing is boring — not to manually reconcile every edge case.

You may be a fit if

  • You’ve shipped a usage-based billing system in production and have opinions on metering architecture, idempotency, and exactly-once semantics.

  • You’ve integrated deeply with Stripe, understand its data model, and have dealt with erroring webhooks.

  • You’ve built or maintained a financial ledger and understand why it’s required.

  • You care about correctness and making sure customer’s don’t have to manually review their invoices.

  • You can hold the tension between "move fast" and "do not lose revenue or trust."

descriptionHtml:

About the role

You embed directly with customer teams as the engineer on the ground: own an outcome, ship a production-grade SpaceXSI system that still runs after you leave, and become the critical technical feedback loop from the field back to product engineering.

The work is the project. One week you might take a messy business workflow and put a production agent on it: pick the use case, stand up the architecture, wire it into the customer’s auth, data, and tools, then harden it with evals until the team actually uses it. Another week you might live in a customer’s repo and delivery system and ship an agent-powered path for a migration, a PR review loop, or an incident-to-fix flow, behind tests, review, and rollout rather than in a chat sidebar. Either way, you measure what matters, leave the customer able to operate it, and bring the pattern back as another use case for SpaceXSI.

This is not a demo role. You own the work end to end, from the first discovery call through launch, iteration, and post-launch support, and you are responsible for systems that work in the real world.

What you’ll do

  • Lead discovery with the customer: orient in their codebases and workflows, find the real bottleneck and the use case worth building, and define clear success metrics

  • Design and ship production agents, AI applications, and coding-agent workflows on Grok and our models, on live business processes and inside the customer’s engineering org

  • Get a first version live in days, then harden it over weeks with rollout, monitoring, and iteration from real usage

  • Own production quality: tracing, evals, debugging model or delivery failures, and latency and cost tradeoffs

  • Build the systems around the model (tools, MCP servers, retrieval, rules, skills, CI gates, and evals) and integrate them into the customer’s auth, data, workflow, and delivery systems; decide when prompting, architecture, data, process, or a model change is the right lever

  • Measure the outcome that matters (revenue, cost, hours saved, error rate, cycle time, escaped defects), not seat adoption

  • Work directly with Staff+, platform, and domain leaders, going deep in their systems while communicating clearly about tradeoffs and results

  • Leave the customer team able to run what you built, and turn what you learn into reusable patterns and improvements to SpaceXSI products

You may be a fit if

  • Required

    • You have 5+ years of experience in software engineering, machine learning engineering, or data science

    • You write and review production code (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript; other languages welcome)

    • You’ve owned a customer or operator outcome, not just a slide or a prototype, and can turn a fuzzy problem into a scoped, shipped system

    • You’ve built and owned AI-native workflows or agents in production, and debugged real production failures (model, tool, data, pipeline, or delivery path)

    • You’ve handled production reliability: metrics, alerts, safe rollouts, incident response

    • You build end to end: frontend, backend, infra, and prompt iteration

    • You thrive in ambiguity and don’t need a complete spec before you start building

    • You can talk to working engineers and to a VP

    Nice to have

    • 2+ years in a customer-facing role, leading discovery conversations and being accountable for outcomes for external stakeholders

    • Hands-on depth in several of: agents and tool-calling, eval harnesses, retrieval and context systems, CI/CD or developer platforms, and AI-native coding workflows in a real repo

    • Experience as a forward-deployed, solutions, or platform engineer embedded with customers, or as a founding engineer who owned an AI product end to end

descriptionHtml:

Software Engineer, RL Data

About the Role

The data behind a model shapes it more than almost anything else. On the RL Data team at SpaceXAI, you decide what that data is for our agents: which problems they practice, what world they practice in, and how they're judged. You'll take a weakness, like an agent that gives up on hard bugs or misuses a calendar API, and turn it into training data that fixes it, then show the next model is measurably better.

You form hypotheses about why data is helping or misleading the model, build the systems to test them, run ablations, and read the rollouts to find the bug, shortcut or mismatch behind a result. Every flaw you catch, or miss, shows up in what the next Grok models learn.

What you’ll work on

  • Turning a capability gap into thousands of verifiable tasks — for example, planting subtle bugs deep in a real project's dependencies for the agent to root-cause.

  • Building environments that behave like production: real codebases with their real dependencies, and simulations of apps like email, calendar, and docs that match the real ones down to search, errors, and pagination.

  • Designing graders for open-ended work that separate good solutions from bad without penalizing valid alternatives or rewarding shortcuts.

  • Building automated checks that catch reward hacking, leaked answers, broken environments, and paths the real product wouldn't allow, before data reaches training.

  • Scaling from a thousand hand-checked tasks to millions, with filters and judges you can trust in place of a person reading each one

You may be a fit if

  • You have strong software engineering fundamentals, and you've built non-trivial systems in Python: data pipelines, test or eval infrastructure, sandboxes, or backend services.

  • You have taste for what makes an environment trustworthy: faithful enough that skills transfer, strict enough that shortcuts fail, and simple enough to debug when a result looks wrong.

  • You are careful and systematic — understanding both aggregate metrics and close reading of raw outputs.

  • You enjoy turning messy, open-ended problems into repeatable, high-quality data production systems.

  • RL or ML experience is a plus but not required. We welcome strong engineers who want to do research on what makes models better.

Applying

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

About the role

SpaceXAI ships fast. New models, new agentic capabilities, new workflows every week. The gap between what Cursor can do and what developers know how to build with it grows with every release. This role closes that gap, one lab, workshop, and tutorial at a time.

As a Product Education Engineer, you'll build the technical content and hands-on experiences that move developers from first install to deep, durable fluency. Code walkthroughs, labs, reference implementations, workshops, in-product learning, and whatever new formats we invent as we go. The demos and tutorials you ship should be things you built by pushing Cursor to its limits in your own work.

This is not a traditional customer education role. We're hiring engineers who teach, not curriculum developers who need external SMEs to write for them. You'll be the SME. You'll go deep on the product, deep with customers, and deep with the engineers building Cursor. You'll be the internal source of truth our Field Engineers, ADMs, and Solutions Architects come to when the product changes and they need to get up to speed.

You'll report to the Director of Product Education Engineering and partner with our Learning Experience Design team, who will help you translate technical depth into content that actually teaches.

What you’ll do

  • Build Cursor's technical learning library hands-on: code walkthroughs, tutorials, labs, workshops, reference implementations, and instructor-led training

  • Build high-quality demos, reference implementations, and workflow automations, using Cursor itself as part of your development process

  • Lead large-format workshops, technical deep dives, and hands-on enablement sessions that help engineering organizations adopt AI coding tools effectively and drive measurable outcomes

  • Be the technical translation layer between Product and the field. When SpaceXAI ships new capabilities, our Field Engineers, ADMs, and Solutions Architects come to you to get up to speed

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, DevRel, and Go-to-Market ahead of major launches so new capabilities ship with clear educational framing, practical examples, and adoption paths on day one

  • Contribute technical guides, patterns, and best practices to Cursor's public technical content to help the broader developer community accelerate their work with Cursor

  • Design learning experiences for both developers and non-technical users (e.g. eng leaders evaluating rollout, PMs pairing with agents). Enterprise adoption depends on both, and our content has to meet each audience on its own terms

  • Experiment with new formats for education, including in-product learning, hands-on labs, interactive experiences, live teaching, and AI-native tutorials (e.g. guided flows that adapt to repo context and skill level)

  • Bring field signal back to Product and Engineering on where developers get stuck and what would unlock the next stage of adoption

  • Measure what works, tracking adoption and fluency gains rather than completion rates

You may be a fit if

  • You have 5+ years of experience in Field Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Consulting, technical enablement, or software engineering at a developer tools or platform company

  • You have a deep understanding of the software development lifecycle, modern engineering org structures, and how AI coding tools are reshaping how software gets built

  • You have a point of view on what makes engineers more productive

  • You care about customer success and operational excellence as much as you care about technical ingenuity

One of our north stars is a future where teams can hire Grok as a remote colleague. Reaching that future requires training our models in realistic, diverse environments that support complex, end-to-end work across domains.

As a Software Engineer on the RL Environments team at SpaceXAI, you’ll build the systems that turn real-world data into high-quality environments and tasks for reinforcement learning. You’ll create dramatically more realistic training environments while owning the shared platforms and quality layers that help us produce trustworthy data quickly and at scale.

This role sits at the intersection of research, data, and engineering. You’ll work closely with ML Platform and research teams to turn company data, Grok Bot interactions, vendor-built tasks, tutor data, acquired data, and synthetic data into training-ready environments. Your work will make high-quality RL data easier to create, validate, discover, and use across our model-training efforts.

What you’ll work on

  • Building platforms that allows us to build complex, realistic, and diverse RL environments at scale, that support end-to-end tasks across knowledge-work domains.

  • Designing end-to-end factory that turns massive raw data into useful and realistic environments.

  • Defining and applying consistent quality standards across vendor, tutor, acquired, and synthetic data.

  • Creating self-serve APIs and tooling that accelerate task and environment development for internal teams and external contributors.

  • Partnering across research, platform, and external teams to translate model-capability goals into effective training tasks and environments.

You may be a fit if

Applying

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

As a Solutions Architect, you’ll work with some of the world’s most sophisticated organizations to answer a new question: what should a company look like when AI agents become part of how work gets done?

We’re hiring Solutions Architects to help strategic customers make AI-native work real in production on the Grok platform, using Grok Bot for knowledge work and business workflows and Grok Build (Cursor) for AI-native software development.

The best Solutions Architects pair technical credibility with product instincts and extreme ownership, and they are as comfortable debugging a CI workflow or leading an architecture review as helping executives, from CTOs to the CRO, CMO, CFO, and COO, understand where AI changes how the business runs and how software is built.

  • Deep expertise in multi-touch attribution, including designing and owning a model end to end and explaining its trade-offs to stakeholders

You’ll work across ticketing workflows, routing logic, queue health, labeling taxonomy, escalation paths, workforce signals, and internal tooling requests.

The ideal person is more technical than a traditional operations lead, more hands-on than a traditional TPM, and less software-engineering-heavy than a dedicated SWE. You should be comfortable investigating messy operational issues, making or coordinating safe system changes, pushing back on unclear requests, and turning recurring problems into durable improvements.

What you’ll do

  • Own day-to-day operations for core support systems, including ticketing workflows, routing, queues, labels, taxonomy, escalations, and related tooling.

  • Triage urgent operational issues as they arise, especially when system behavior, workforce distribution, queue health, or SLA risk looks off.

  • Manage intake, prioritization, and follow-through for systems requests from support managers, TSEs, operations leads, engineering, product, and other internal teams.

  • Help maintain the team’s roadmap by distinguishing one-off fixes from broader system improvements, surfacing recurring pain points, and pushing back on low-leverage work.

  • Drive smaller technical and operational programs end-to-end, being responsible for discovery, scoping and execution, rollout, documentation and success metrics.

  • Partner with engineering, data, IT, and support leaders to debug issues, validate changes, improve monitoring, and prevent repeat failures.

  • Use Cursor and AI-native workflows to reduce manual toil, investigate issues, summarize signals, draft documentation, test changes, and improve how the team operates.

You may be a fit if

  • You have experience in support operations, systems operations, technical program management, or a similarly cross-functional technical systems role.

  • You are comfortable working close to operational systems such as ticketing platforms, routing workflows, queue configuration, labels/taxonomies, dashboards, Slack workflows, and internal tools.

  • You are technical enough to investigate system issues, read configuration or code, and partner effectively with engineers, even if you are not primarily a software engineer.

  • You are excellent at triage and prioritization: when several things are broken or ambiguous, you can quickly determine what is urgent, what needs investigation, what needs escalation, and what should become a longer-term fix.

  • You can own work end to end: clarify the problem, align stakeholders, sequence the work, communicate tradeoffs, launch safely, and measure whether the change worked.

  • You are comfortable pushing back thoughtfully and can tell stakeholders “not yet,” “not this way,” or “this should be part of a broader fix” while maintaining trust.

  • You are energized by a role that blends firefighting with systems-building, and you have a strong bias toward action, clarity, and continuous improvement.

• Own the in-market partner business from concept to completion. Set the market partner strategy and sequencing from greenfield, then execute it personally.

• Accelerate SpaceXSI's global partners into your market and incubate them to productivity, across Technology and Transformation partnerships.

• Where gaps exist, recruit, onboard, and manage local partners from the ground up.

• Build and run co-sell motions, stand up FDE (forward deployed engineer) capacity, and drive C-level access and value-amplification programs through to landed wins.

• Turn partner relationships into qualified pipeline and closed co-sell revenue that feeds the in-market Japan President's number.

• You have professional working proficiency in English. You will engage consistently with HQ and present plans to English-speaking stakeholders, so you can operate and communicate confidently in English. Fluency in both Japanese and English is the highest-value combination for this role.

• You are a builder-operator, a doer rather than a coordinator, energized by owning a business from greenfield and running it as it grows.

title: Forward Deployed Strategist
descriptionHtml:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

About the role

We're looking for a Forward Deployed Strategist to own our most strategic customer engagements - from first workshop through delivery. You'll sit with executive sponsors, surface the highest-value use cases, turn them into tightly scoped projects, then stay accountable for the outcome, working with the FDE.

You'll typically work in a pod of one Strategist and 1-2 FDEs. You own the executive relationship and the shape of delivery; the FDE embeds with the customer's team and owns the deeper production builds. You'll stay hands-on at the configuration layer week to week, including workflows, integrations, and platform tooling, partnering with the FDE where the build is most complex. You will translate technical build into business outcomes and own the adoption of the build.

This is for someone who combines technical credibility in agentic coding and LLMs with the executive presence to earn trust in the boardroom, and the judgment to keep engagements scoped tight, delivered fast, and worth repeating.

What you’ll do

  • Scope

    • Partner with customer executive sponsors to scope FDE projects — translating ambiguous business problems into concrete, time-boxed deliverables with clear ROI

    • Lead technical discovery and architecture reviews, surfacing integration complexity and infrastructure constraints to validate that every engagement is technically feasible

    Deliver

    • Work side by side with the FDE on the technical build — you own the configuration layer including workflows, settings, integrations, and platform tooling that don't require heavy custom code while the FDE owns the deeper production builds

    • Own technical enablement and adoption: run hands-on training, build playbooks and reference workflows, and coach the customer's team until they're self-sufficient. Adoption is measured by what their users do without you in the room

    • Monitor technical feasibility throughout delivery, adjusting scope with the sponsor when constraints emerge rather than letting engagements drift

    • Identify and scope expansion opportunities as they surface during delivery, in partnership with the account team

    • Escalate product gaps, integration friction, and recurring customer pain back to Product and Engineering with enough specificity to drive roadmap decisions

    • Build reusable playbooks that make the broader FDE org more capable over time

    Own the executive relationship

    • Establish and maintain the executive relationship on your engagements, serving as the primary point of contact from kickoff through handoff

    • Sell the vision and the plan to C-suite stakeholders who need to believe in both the outcome and the team delivering it

    • Translate between business outcomes and technical implementation in both directions — for the sponsor and for the build team

You may be a fit if

  • You've spent 6+ years in Solutions Architecture, Deployment Strategy, technical consulting, or an Engagement Manager seat where you owned scoping and delivery with a technical team in AI-production workflows

  • You understand agentic coding and LLMs well enough to hold your own with senior eng: how they behave in production, where they fail, and what a resilient workflow looks like (you don't need to be the person writing the production code)

  • You're comfortable hands-on with Grok workflows, integrations, and platform config, and can read enough Python / JS-TS to partner with an FDE

  • You've shipped AI-native workflows past the prototype stage and can tell a real production constraint from a nice-to-have

  • You can walk into an unfamiliar enterprise eng org, find the highest-leverage intervention fast, and scope something that delivers concrete value in weeks, not quarters

  • You have the executive presence to own the C-suite relationship and the technical credibility to earn trust with their eng leads

  • Domain depth in FSI, insurance, telecom, high-tech, healthcare/life sciences, or semiconductor is a strong plus

You'll also build our partner FDE track — training and enabling GSI and consulting partners who extend this motion at scale.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who combines deep technical credibility, strong people management, and the judgment to keep engagements scoped tight, delivered fast, and worth repeating.

What you’ll do

  • Sell

    • Own the full arc from technical discovery to executive close — partnering with Sales and Account teams to qualify opportunities, leading architecture reviews, surfacing integration complexity and infrastructure constraints, and scoping engagements with enough precision to de-risk delivery before a line of code is written

    • Build and present proposals that translate ambiguous customer problems into concrete, time-boxed deliverables with clear ROI

    • Sell the vision and the plan to C-suite stakeholders who need to believe in both the outcome and the team delivering it

    • Drive deal strategy on strategic accounts; your technical credibility is a direct lever on close rates for six- and seven-figure engagements

    Deliver

    • Serve as executive technical sponsor on your region's highest-priority engagements and manage stakeholder relationships from IC engineers to C-suite

    • Ensure delivery quality across your team's projects: appropriate scoping, milestone tracking, technical standards, and clean handoffs to customer engineering teamsTranslate between business outcomes and technical implementation in both directions

    • Identify and escalate product gaps, integration friction, and recurring customer pain back to Product and Engineering with enough specificity to drive roadmap decisions

    • Manage active engagements: escalate on complex builds, coach FDEs on scoping and delivery decisions, and step in directly on accounts where the stakes are highest

    • Build reusable playbooks that make the broader FDE org more capable over time

    Manage People

    • Lead, develop, and scale a team of 6–8 Forward Deployed Engineers working strategic FDE projects

    • Hire top-tier FDE talent; set clear expectations, technical performance standards, and career growth paths for a team where "excellent" means actually shipping in production

    • Coach FDEs through the hardest problems in the field — scoping under deal pressure, building alongside senior technical stakeholders, and knowing when to protect scope vs. when to flex

    • Build and scale the partner FDE track — train, enable, and hold the quality bar for GSI and consulting partners who carry the FDE motion forward at volume

You may be a fit if

  • You have 8+ years of experience leading technical teams that build and ship in production — Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Engineering, or a similar function where writing and reviewing code is part of the job

  • You have experience with software development and coding in Python, Javascript/Typescript

  • You’ve built and owned AI-native workflows in production, not just prototypes, and have debugged real-world model failures

About the Role

As a Solutions Architect, you’ll work with some of the world’s most sophisticated organizations to answer a new question: what should a company look like when AI agents become part of how work gets done?

We’re hiring Solutions Architects to help strategic customers make AI-native work real in production on the Grok platform, using Grok Bot for knowledge work and business workflows and Grok Build (Cursor) for AI-native software development. This role will be based in Sydney.

This is a hands-on technical role within the Customer Success organization, where you’ll partner with AI Deployment Managers (ADMs) to own the technical track across architecture, workflow redesign, and enterprise security while helping organizations rethink how they operate and how they build software with AI.

You’ll help customers move from excitement to workflows teams rely on every day by discovering real job friction, integrating Grok Build into codebases, CI pipelines, and code review, and designing scoped Grok Bot workflows with human-in-the-loop judgment.

The best Solutions Architects pair technical credibility with product instincts and extreme ownership, and they are as comfortable debugging a CI workflow or leading an architecture review as helping executives, from CTOs to the CRO, CMO, CFO, and COO, understand where AI changes how the business runs and how software is built.

What You’ll Do

Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development with Grok Build (Cursor)

  • Roll out Grok Build across strategic engineering organizations and integrate it into real codebases and production workflows rather than isolated demos.

  • Configure developer environments, repository rules, and conventions, and run hands-on enablement that drives fast, durable adoption.

  • Bring agentic SDLC practices into the customer’s delivery process, from planning and implementation through testing, CI, and code review, and clear developer workflow friction along the way.

  • Keep a strong hands-on Build baseline by shipping runnable, convention-driven work in Grok Build yourself.

Engage Customers on the Grok Bot Journey

  • Use Grok Bot to turn a business user’s problem into an accepted user story and requirements that flow into Jira and through the agentic SDLC in Grok Build.

  • Lead discovery for knowledge-work and business-process use cases and redesign high-value workflows around AI agents, enterprise tools, data, and human judgment.

  • Help customers operationalize agents with ownership, integrations, and guardrails.

Expand Across the Organization

  • Establish a data governance and security framework that lets leadership adopt the Grok platform top down across the enterprise.

  • Help engineering organizations move from isolated usage to company-wide adoption by turning successful deployments into reusable patterns and rollouts for new teams and platform groups.

  • Partner with ADMs and Account Executives to find and drive major expansion opportunities for the Grok platform.

Become a Trusted Technical Partner

  • Build multi-threaded relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering and business leaders, and executive sponsors, and turn skeptics into champions.

  • Lead architecture reviews and working sessions, and advise on what to build, developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and adoption strategy.

  • Prototype alongside customers by connecting systems, designing agents and workflows, and debugging failures until ambiguous ideas become working systems.

  • Reason about trust boundaries with CISOs and platform owners, covering identity, permissions, data access, connectors and MCPs, execution environments, network controls, auditability, and human approval, and know when to escalate to specialists.

  • Partner with ADMs from meeting prep through active participation, and coordinate with Sales, Product, and Engineering to unblock customers.

Drive Real Customer Outcomes

  • Translate adoption into measurable impact, from faster iteration, developer productivity, and engineering quality to workflow efficiency, and help customers communicate that value internally.

  • Help teams standardize on the Grok platform and embed it deeply in core workflows, and lead recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction.

Shape the Future of the Product

  • Bring structured feedback, emerging patterns, and enterprise requirements across Grok Bot and Grok Build from strategic customers into Product and Engineering.

  • Shape new capabilities alongside lighthouse customers whose deployments set the standard for the market.

You Might Be a Fit If

  • You have deep technical foundations across APIs, software architecture, cloud infrastructure, data, identity, security, and enterprise integrations, often from a software engineering, FDE, SA, platform, developer tooling, or business-process automation background.

  • You have a strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, continuous integration and delivery systems, code review, and enterprise engineering environments, ideally with hands-on experience in Cursor or similar AI coding tools.

  • You bring customer-facing technical experience as an SA, SE, FDE, TAM, enterprise architect, or integration consultant, working hands-on with engineering teams while operating strategically with technical leadership.

  • You bring high drive, ownership, curiosity, adaptability, and systems thinking, along with strong prep habits and comfort in fast-moving ambiguity.

  • You have experience designing workflows that span tools, data, APIs, and human processes, not only IDE-centric developer workflows.

  • You bring a working grasp of security and compliance, or a clear path to one, and can walk customers through scenario-based guardrails.

  • You have excellent communication skills across technical, executive, and business audiences and strong instincts for discovery, workflow design, and adoption strategy.

  • You bring a passion for developer tooling and for how AI will reshape software engineering and knowledge work.

  • You bring a willingness to travel to customers as needed.
